citation: Niu et al., RAGTruth: A Hallucination Corpus for Developing Trustworthy Retrieval-Augmented Language Models, arXiv:2401.00396

subtlety.note: carried on the case's gold spans, never a code

implicit_true.note: the annotators' 'true but not in the source' facet; metadata only

due_to_null.note: data-to-text spans caused by a null field; metadata only

verdict_rule.ragtruth: a response is hallucinated iff it carries at least one annotated span (any type)
verdict_rule.lithrim: a case is BLOCK iff at least one Tier-1 finding stands after the floor; both codes are Tier-1, so any mapped span => BLOCK

untyped_prediction_class: hallucination (untyped span; the paper's detection prompt emits spans without a type, so it is scored at response and span level only, never per code)
admissibility: a RAGTruth label_type with no code above fails ingest; a response with no spans is a first-class clean negative (expected_safety_flags: [])
